title: Delta audit export with role-aware masking and session-context pagination
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Implement an incremental (delta) export capability for the Audit Console that streams CSV/JSON rows since a recorded cursor, applies RBAC v2-aware field masking, and preserves session-level context for SSO/SAML identities. This ticket covers the backend export API, export-format templates, permission-aware redaction rules, and the Console UX to trigger and monitor delta exports.

Why this work: Customers with high-volume audit data need periodic exports for compliance (SIEM ingestion) without re-downloading full archives. Current exports are full snapshots or ad-hoc filtered downloads which are costly and create duplication. We must ensure exports never leak fields blocked by RBAC v2 (service tokens, sensitive headers, raw request bodies) and that exported rows include stable session identifiers (SSO/SAML subject + session_id) where allowed.

Goals:
- Provide an authenticated export API endpoint that accepts a named saved query + start_cursor and streams delta results in CSV or JSONL.
- Apply role-aware masking rules at export time: redact or pseudonymize fields based on the requesting principal's permissions under RBAC v2.
- Include session context columns: saml_subject (if permitted), session_id, ip_geolocation (coarse).
- Support server-side cursor checkpoints for resumable exports and automatic rotation for long-running jobs.
- UX: Console shows export job status, bytes written, errors, and download (S3 presigned) or streaming websocket option.

Out of scope: full row-level encryption for exported files (will be a follow-up); long-term cold storage lifecycle management.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- We will implement deterministic pseudonymization for IDs (HMAC with per-customer key) instead of full irreversible hashing to allow safe internal joining and debugging under strict audit. This balances usefulness and privacy.
- Rather than building a bespoke query engine, we will reuse the existing audit search pipeline and add a streaming serializer layer to avoid duplication of indexing logic. This reduces dev time but requires careful backpressure handling.
- For high-volume exports, we will favor server-side batching and S3 multipart upload rather than trying to stream large files directly to the browser. A small streaming websocket option will be kept for low-volume ad-hoc downloads.

Acceptance criteria:
- API: POST /api/v2/audit/exports starts a job and returns job_id and checkpoint cursor.
- API: GET /api/v2/audit/exports/{job_id}/status returns status, rows_exported, bytes, errors.
- Export formats: CSV with header row and JSONL; both validated against schema.
- RBAC: Users with role.viewer_export see masked values for fields flagged sensitive; role.audit_admin sees unmasked fields.
- Resumability: Jobs can be resumed from last recorded checkpoint within 48h window.
- E2E tests: integration tests covering role combinations and SSO subject inclusion.
- Console UX: Saved-query selector + checkbox for "delta since last checkpoint" and download link when complete.

Design artifacts and references:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RINF/Audit+Delta+Export
- Spec: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a-DeltaExportSpec (internal link placeholder)
- GitHub proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4321
- Datadog dashboard (export job metrics): https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/abcd-export-jobs

Notes on security review: The export pipeline touches sensitive event payloads and will require a security signoff before GA. We will run threat-modeling with Security and Privacy to validate pseudonymization and key-handling for HMAC seeds.

Next steps: finalize redaction matrix with PM and Security, implement streaming serializer, add job persistence + checkpointing, wire Console UX, run tenant-canary for 2 low-volume customers, and schedule security review.
acceptance_criteria: Start export job accepts saved_query_id and start_cursor and returns job_id and initial cursor
Role-aware masking: export responses apply redaction rules per RBAC v2 policy
Support CSV and JSONL with schema validation tests
Resumable exports: job can be resumed from last checkpoint within 48h
Console shows export progress and provides S3 download or streaming websocket for small results
comments: 2026-02-16 - Aisha: Drafted scope and initial design. Spoke with Security about pseudonymization; they prefer HMAC using KMS-managed key. Open question: per-tenant key or global key?

2026-02-20 - Marcelo: Backend spike done. Reused audit-search scroll API and added streaming serializer; discovered high memory when buffering CSV headers for dynamic columns. Will switch to column schema discovery pass then stream rows.
2026-02-28 - Design review (Lina Chen): UX mockups uploaded to Confluence and linked. PM asked to include ability to save export presets. Added label saved_presets.
2026-03-04 - Security review kickoff: threat model session scheduled. Security requested explicit handling of SAML attributes — must not include raw SAML assertions in exports.
2026-03-08 - Dev note: Implemented HMAC pseudonymization using KMS-encrypted salt per org; PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4321
2026-03-11 - QA: found bug where session_id column duplicated when saved query includes session grouping; added fix to serializer. Running regression suite.
2026-03-12 - Marcelo: Ready for internal demo. Will request security signoff and trigger tenant-canary next week.
implementation_notes: Streaming: use existing search scroll cursor + gasket to translate into CSV/JSONL rows to minimize re-querying index
Masking: evaluate using server-side policy engine that maps RBAC roles to field-level actions (allow/ redact/ pseudonymize)
Checkpoint persistence: store last processed event id and timestamp in export_jobs table; TTL 48h for resumability
Large exports: write to S3 with multipart upload; generate presigned URL and mark job complete when upload finished
Testing: add integration tests with two simulated tenants and varying RBAC policies to validate masking
